prompt: Create three questions for a private workshop demonstration, in English. Use only these chapter facts: training updates model parameters; ordinary inference keeps parameters fixed; a new prompt changes context; RAG supplies retrieved passages as context. Q1 Multiple Choice: During ordinary inference, what changes when a new prompt is entered? Options: A The original training data; B The available context; C The learned parameters. Correct answer B, 1 point. Q2 Free Response: Andrea says that adding a definition to the prompt updates the model weights. Explain the error in two sentences. Expected: context changes, learned parameters remain fixed during ordinary inference. Q3 Drawing: Draw and label prompt plus context -> inference with fixed parameters -> next token. Add a brief note explaining what changes when a definition is added. Use only these three basic question types. This is an authored example; no real student records.
observed: Created three questions with Luna: multiple choice, free response and drawing; verified B as the multiple-choice key; removed all six generated hints and the optional Show your work feature; previewed all three learner response formats.
scope: Recorded in an automatically enabled Paid Teacher trial, using the three basic question types. Premium rubric integration was not enabled. The initial AI proposal added an extra distractor, hints and Show your work; teacher review removed the optional hints and Show your work. No activity was assigned to real students.

name: Plan a lesson around independent explanation
prompt: Plan a 20-minute university lesson using the workshop chapter on training, inference and RAG. Goal: independently explain what changes in each process. Include a diagnostic question, a short source-reading activity, a labelled diagram, a misconception check and a two-minute exit ticket. Give timings and expected evidence. Source distinctions: training updates numerical parameters; ordinary inference keeps the learned parameters fixed; prompt changes affect context; RAG retrieves passages and adds them to context, without itself retraining the model. Include a simpler prompt for a learner who confuses context with parameters, keeping the same learning goal.
observed: Generated a 20-minute lesson with a 2/4/5/7/2-minute sequence, learner evidence, a simpler prompt and an accurate exit-ticket key; copied the editable document text.
scope: Actual MagicSchool execution on authored workshop distinctions. The plan is a draft for teacher review. The diagnostic wording “inside the model” needs clarification; an individual diagnostic check is retained before source work. No classroom learning effect was measured. Account plan not established.
